Hello! Welcome back to the Cozy Corner Library! Another Monday, another week and its time again to grab your beverage of choice, sit down and listen to the literary gems we will present to you today. I'm Beth Burton, long time host and book lover and as always with me is my wonderful co-host Darren Williams.

atoms.a: The speaker introduces a weekly book podcast.

instruction.sound: Yes, thank you Beth! This weeks episode is going to be all about classic Victorian horror. Sounds spooky! Our special guests for today are book blogger James Chang and fantasy author Henrietta Mauville.

atoms.a: The host introduces the classic authors they will talk about on this episode.

wrong.text: He introduces the topic of the episode and two guests of the podcast.

instruction.text: Assign the person who holds this opinion on Mary Shelley's Frankenstein:
instruction.sound: Assign the person who holds this opinion on Mary Shelley's Frankenstein.

cards.sound: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f2Us_chirp'>Mary Shelley's Frankenstein truly had such a huge cultural impact. The story has influenced literature, film, and popular culture for over two centuries. Even people who haven’t read the book recognize the idea of “Frankenstein’s monster.”</voice>

<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m1Us_chirp'>The novel raises powerful questions about responsibility, ambition, and the dangers of pursuing knowledge without thinking about the consequences. It feels remarkable that a book written in the early 1800s still speaks so clearly to modern debates about science and ethics.</voice>

<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m4Au_chirp'>For me, Frankenstein's creature is the most compelling part of the novel. Mary Shelley gives him emotional depth and intelligence, which makes his loneliness and rejection genuinely tragic. He was not born a monster but shaped by isolation and cruelty.</voice>

<voice voiceLang='en' voice='f3_chirp'>I really admire the way Shelley structured her book. The layered narrative frames Victor’s story and the creature’s perspective as two sides of the same coin. When the creature tells his own story, it completely reshapes the reader’s view of him and of Victor’s actions. This makes us readers really question the truth of narration.</voice>

atoms.a: “The creature's perspective reframes the way readers understand the story's events.”
atoms.sound: The creature's perspective reframes the way readers understand the story's events.

instruction.text: You will hear an opinion about Emily Brontë's Wuthering Heights. Tick all statements that correctly reflect what has been said. Multiple answers may be correct.
instruction.sound: You will hear an opinion about Emily Brontës Wuthering Heights. Tick all statements that correctly reflect what has been said. Multiple answers may be correct.

atoms.sound: Wuthering Heights surprised me because it isn’t really a romantic classic but a psychological drama about obsession, cruelty, and social exclusion. What stood out most to me is how Heathcliff is repeatedly described as dark‑skinned and treated as an outsider, which shapes much of the conflict. Characters insult him with racialised language and treat him as socially inferior, and that rejection fuels his bitterness and relentless revenge. His destructive devotion to Catherine feels less like idealized love and more like the result of lifelong humiliation and isolation. Although the characters can be frustratingly selfish, Brontës refusal to moralise makes the novel powerful.

b: ++James challenges the notion that the novel is a classic romance.
Heathcliff's character is shaped only by classist abuse.
Catherine and Heathcliff's love is moralised and idealised in the novel.
++James presents the book as a psychological drama.
++The book narrates destructive relationships shaped by systems of class, gender, race and society.

hint.label: Vocabulary

atoms.sound: What stood out to me most when reading Bram Stoker's Dracula was how the vampire himself represents a frightening outsider who disrupts Victorian society. The horror of the novel is tied to Victorian anxieties about sexuality and loss of social control. Dracula’s ability to seduce and corrupt reflects fears about uncontrolled desire and the breakdown of moral boundaries. When Dracula and three other vampiric women bite and seduce Jonathan Harker, the scene blurs lines between pleasure and danger, marking intimacy itself a transgression.

b: Lucy’s transformation restores the social order of Victorian society.
++Henrietta links the novel’s horror to Victorian anxieties about sexuality and social control.
++Sexual intimacy is portrayed as a kind of moral transgression in the novel.
Violence and intimacy are unrelated in the narrative.

cats.sound: Wow, thank you so much. I really feel I've learned a lot today! While I've been a lover of horror, I truly haven't dived into these amazing classics yet. I will definitely pick up Dracula now! Can you believe that I've seen so many movie adaptations but never read the book. Gotta change that immediately.

Indeed, I have enjoyed our little book time again. Until now, I had classed Wuthering Heights into the romance genre but I sure feel wrong on that now! So much more complex than what I'd thought. Still, a brooding male protagonist gets me anytime. Anyway, I hope you all feel inspired and want to pick up one of these classics soon.

atoms.sound: I have not yet read any of the classic novels.
I watched multiple film adaptations of this novel.
I feel that I have learned much.
I changed my opinion on this classic's genre.
I hope more people are interested in classic novels now.
